fn-pointer-member-record.meaning: member of a record the lexical reader refuses whole because one member is a function pointer (RECORD-BODY-TOTAL-OR-REJECT); the member-path and typed readings admit the same access on any record the reader reads

fn-pointer-parameter-function.meaning: every declaration of a function is unread because one formal is a function pointer (the declaration reader's ParameterListToken refusal); the typed readings admit the same accesses in any function whose declarations are read

callback-member-call.meaning: a call through a function-pointer member (rules 12n/13u: callback member closure), or a test of one; no reader change admits it

logging-macro.meaning: Fluent Bit's logging macros: a nested call (flb_input_name, flb_input_plugin_log_suppress_check) or an array member (`char name[32]`) inside a variadic logging call or its condition (CG05 nested-call effects, array-member decay)

pointer-store-into-member.meaning: a pointer stored into a member of a caller's object or of a fresh object (`config->evl = evl`, `sched->config = config`, `ins->ht_log_chunks = NULL`): the projection keeps a stored formal pointer or a store into a caller's record refused (W45-SUB-OBJECT-STORES, C00)

member-release.meaning: a release or close of an object or descriptor held in a member of a formal outside rule W45-CALLEE-SUMMARY-CASCADE's destructor premises P1-P4 (flb_sds_destroy(ins->alias), cmt_destroy(ins->cmt), close of a member-held descriptor)

member-descriptor-slots.meaning: addresses of a member's descriptor array elements handed to mk_event_channel_create / flb_pipe_create (`&ins->ch_events[0]`): descriptors written into a caller's memory have no identity (C04.6)

uncontracted-call-with-member.meaning: a member actual of a call to a callee with no contract in force (pthread_mutex_lock/unlock, memcpy of a thread id)

interior-address-of-looked-up-record.meaning: the interior address or member of a record obtained by an id lookup or list iteration (`get_collector`, `mk_list_foreach`)

list-or-lookup.meaning: the name is bound by a list iteration, an id lookup or an event-loop iteration

void-thread-argument.meaning: the name is a `void *` thread or callback argument cast to a record pointer: no caller identity crosses pthread_create / mk_utils_worker_spawn

uncontracted-result.meaning: the name is bound to the result of a call with no contract in force on this route

tls-get.meaning: the name is read from thread-local storage (FLB_TLS_GET)

formal-may-bind.meaning: a store or pointer read through a formal the body itself may bind: it releases it (`flb_free(thi)`, `flb_free(ctx)`) or links or unlinks it (`mk_list_add/del(&req->_head, ...)`), so the typed readings' never-bound premise fails and a store through the caller-held record has no identity (C00, store direction)

formal-handed-to-uncontracted-call.meaning: a formal handed whole to a callee with no contract or validated summary on this route (another unit's function, or a same-unit function whose own row is Unknown), which poisons it for every later use

nested-or-condition-call.meaning: a nested call in an actual or a call in a branch condition (CG05 nested-call effects, rule 10y)

after-retention-undecided.meaning: a use of the interior a refused retention named (rule 12t `retention-undecided`): it clears only with the lifetime model (FB-EVENT-LOOP-CROSS-FUNCTION-LIFETIME, S3)

pointer-read-from-member.meaning: a pointer loaded from a member of a formal (`thi = ins->thi`) names no identity the projection tracks; its null test and uses refuse
